scope: Isolated S1 inactive parent, child-started navigation, and pending traversal checkpoint. Four new frame fixtures show a failed frame in a parent that is no longer the view's active document, a navigation that a child frame starts and a pending navigation that fails with it, and a history traversal inside a frame that is pending when its event loop fails. Each runs for a script-thread unwind in the frames part, and for content-process exit and kill in the processes part. The patch needed no change. The parts now have 52, 16, and 41 cases. No product dependency or security configuration changes.

configuration.part_check: Each part runs as its own fixture process. Each part must print exactly its own case markers, ending with its summary marker, and the summary must report its own case count. Each repeat must then cover 68 cases in single-process mode or 109 cases in multiprocess mode, each once.
configuration.notice_check: Every contained case captures the parent's frame notices inside the barrier, while the parent's script thread still waits and the frame cannot navigate. It requires exactly one notice that names the parent's identity, exactly the failed frame's browsing context and failed pipeline, and the exact reason. The failed pipeline is the frame's current pipeline, or the pending pipeline for a failed pending or first navigation. After the error page, the late data, and a 300-millisecond settle, the parent still has exactly one notice. The parent-loop popup, the child-site popup, and the independent view have none. In the same-site pending cases, the parent's own document fails, and neither the parent nor the parent-loop popup has a notice.
configuration.send_check: frame-send-failure loads a cross-site child alone in its own event loop. Inside the parent's barrier, the probe closes the constellation's channel to that event loop and sends one GetTitle message through send_message_to_pipeline. The send fails with the channel's own error. No script thread unwinds and no process exits. The frame's crash details and the notice reason must begin with "Send failed (", which only handle_send_error builds.
configuration.history_check: javascript-url-history-crash-recovery loads a start page and a source page, replaces the source entry with a javascript: URL result, and loads a next page, for three entries. The next page's script thread unwinds. The crash page must report two entries. Back must reach the start page, forward must restore the crash page, and back must reach the start page again. The result text and marker never appear, and every earlier identity is stale.
configuration.dead_send_check: frame-send-dead-thread (frames part, both modes) and frame-send-dead-process (processes part, multiprocess) load a cross-site child alone in its own event loop. Inside the parent's barrier, one probe request ends the child's event loop for real, by the existing script-thread crash message or by SIGKILL to the child's content process, and then calls send_message_to_pipeline with a GetTitle message every two milliseconds until the frame's pipeline is gone or three seconds pass. The constellation handles the request on its own thread, so the panic report and the process lifeline wait in their queues. The probe must report that the frame runs in another event loop than the parent and that a real send failed and closed the pipeline. The frame's crash details and the one notice must begin with "Send failed (", and the parent's other checks match frame-send-failure. After release, error page, late data, and 300 milliseconds, the parent has exactly one notice. The panic report or lifeline then finds no pipeline of the dead event loop.
configuration.group_check: frame-siblings-failure and frame-nested-failure, with their process exit and kill variants, load a parent that runs in another event loop than the failed frames. The siblings parent has a healthy same-origin frame in the parent's own event loop, then two frames of one cross-site origin. The nested parent has one cross-site frame that contains a frame of its own origin. Before the failure, the new probe must show every frame live with no crash details and no pending pipeline, the failed frames in the newest frame's event loop, and, for siblings, the healthy frame in another loop. Inside the parent's barrier the notice must have arrived exactly once, naming the parent's identity and exactly the outermost failed frames with their failed pipelines, in any order, with the exact reason. The failed pipelines must be closed, the healthy frame's record must be unchanged, and the parent must have no revocation, crash notification, or terminal callback. After release, all eight callbacks must succeed in the same document. Each outermost failed frame must then have a new live pipeline with crash details that begin with the reason, in an event loop other than the failed one, with distinct pipelines. A nested frame's browsing context must be absent. The parent's view of its frames, its readiness, and its notices must not change after 300 milliseconds. Reload must load every frame again without crash details, and a new URL must recover.
configuration.inactive_parent_check: frame-inactive-parent-failure, frame-inactive-parent-process-exit, and frame-inactive-parent-process-kill load a parent with one cross-site frame, open a popup that loads the frame's site, and navigate the view to a second page. The probes must show the frame live and absent from the active document's frames. The popup's own failure then ends the shared event loop, with eight callbacks queued on the active document and on the popup, and a popup in the active document's event loop. Inside the barrier, the active document must keep its scope with no revocation, crash notification, or terminal callback, and the view must have exactly one notice that names the active document and the failed frame of the inactive document. That notice is an observed rule. After release, the active document's eight callbacks must succeed, and the frame must have a new live pipeline with crash details that begin with the reason, in another event loop. Back must restore the first document with a new identity, reject the first and second identities, and show the same error page. Reload and a new URL must recover.
configuration.child_navigation_check: frame-child-navigation-failure and frame-child-same-site-navigation-failure, with their process exit and kill variants, load a cross-site child that assigns its own location when the parent posts a message. The host withholds the navigation response, and the probe must show a pending pipeline for the frame, in a third process for the third-site target and in the failed process for the same-site target in multiprocess mode. The child's event loop then fails. The notice must name the frame once with the current pipeline, or in the same-site case with either of its two pipelines. The frame must lose its pending pipeline, get an error page, fire its second load event, and keep one history entry. The late response must change nothing, and the engine must report no error. Reload and a new URL must recover.
configuration.traversal_check: frame-traversal-failure, frame-traversal-process-exit, and frame-traversal-process-kill load a frame with two same-site documents. A first failure ends their event loop, and the frame shows an error page. Back starts a traversal whose pending pipeline the host withholds. The probe must show the first error page current, a pending pipeline, no traversal completion, and one notice. The second failure ends the pending pipeline's event loop. Inside the barrier, the parent must have no revocation, crash notification, or terminal callback, exactly two notices, the second naming the pending pipeline, no pending pipeline, the first error page still current, and the host must have the traversal's completion. After release, a second error page must replace the first, the frame view must report four load events and two history entries, and the late response must change nothing. Further back and forward must complete without changing the frame. Reload and a new URL must recover.

engine_patch.change: None. The patch file is byte-identical to the previous checkpoint's. The experimental constellation behavior already met the required outcomes for a failed frame in an inactive parent, a navigation that the child starts, and a pending traversal inside a frame. The notice for an inactive parent is an observed rule and an open owner decision.

fixture_changes: Delegate gains hold_documents, a list of document paths that the host withholds while listed. The cross-site child branch of load_web_resource serves two new child paths that start their own navigation when their parent posts a message.

FramePath gains ChildNavigation and ChildSameSite. frame_path_failure arms the child's navigation through a parent message, checks the pending process in multiprocess mode, accepts either pipeline in the same-site notice, releases the late response, and checks that reload loads the original child.

frame_inactive_parent_failure and frame_traversal_failure are new functions. The first fails the frame's event loop through a popup of its site, because the frame probes read only the active document's frames.

frame-inactive-parent-failure, frame-child-navigation-failure, frame-child-same-site-navigation-failure, and frame-traversal-failure join the frames part. The processes part gains the exit and kill variants of each, eight cases.
The runner case lists, the document-scope case counts, and the runner test counts change to 52, 16, and 41 cases, with 68 shared and 109 multiprocess cases.
findings: The current patch needs no change for any of the three layouts. A failure of a frame's event loop in an inactive parent, with a child's own navigation pending, or with a traversal pending inside the frame leaves the parent's document, scope, retained reply, and eight held callbacks intact. It sends no crash notification, and it gives each outermost failed frame an error page in a new event loop.

A failed frame in an inactive parent keeps its error page when back restores the parent. The restored parent has a new identity, the engine rejects the first and second parents' identities, and no dead pipeline returns. In this layout, the one frame failure notice names the active document, while the failed frame belongs to the inactive document. No recorded owner decision covers this notice. The fixture asserts the observed notice and labels it so.

A navigation that the child starts closes with the failed frame. The joint session history gains no entry, the late response reaches no live document, and the engine reports no error. When the pending pipeline shares the failed event loop, the frame has two failed pipelines, and the notice names the frame once with one of them. The fixture accepts either and records the one named. In the final runs the notice named the pending pipeline for the script-thread unwind and the child exit, and the current pipeline for the host SIGKILL, the same in all three repeats. In development runs against an earlier preparation, which asserted the current pipeline alone, it named the current pipeline in script-thread runs of that preparation. The panic handler takes whichever of the frame's pipelines it visits first while iterating an FxHashMap with unspecified order, so the choice is unspecified and varied between runs and preparations. The crash load of the frame takes that pipeline's load data, so which load an error page would repeat on reload depends on the same order. The contract does not choose.

A pending traversal inside a frame is a pending pipeline of the existing frame. Its failure produces a second notice and a second error page that replaces the first. The constellation drops the closed pipeline from the ongoing traversal, so the host receives the traversal's completion even though the parent's script thread waits. Further back and forward complete without changing the frame, which is the observed rule.

An attempt to isolate the traversal case by removing the constellation's drop of closed pending pipelines from ongoing traversals was not a control. That drop is also the completion path of every traversal that activates normally. The attempt reached the fixture deadline in earlier cases: the documents part after 27 cases, the frames part after 7, and the processes part after 10. Its logs were not retained. The retained control treats a reloading pending pipeline as a history pipeline instead.

timing_observations.note: The runner times each part's whole process, including engine startup and shutdown. The multiprocess frames part grew from 31.3 to 31.6 seconds to 45.1 to 45.3 seconds, and the processes part from 18.9 to 19.0 seconds to 27.1 to 27.2 seconds, for four new cases and eight new cases. The single-process frames part grew from 9.5 to 9.7 seconds to 12.9 to 13.0 seconds. This checkpoint keeps all fixture and runner deadlines. The margins to the 80-second multiprocess fixture deadline are about 42, 35, and 53 seconds for the documents, frames, and processes parts. The single-process frames part has about 17 seconds to its 30-second deadline.

negative_controls.name: inactive-parent-skip
negative_controls.variation: The final patch, with contained_failed_frames skipping any frame whose parent pipeline is not the current pipeline of its browsing context, so only frames of active documents get an error page. Everything else, including the fixture, is final.

engine_overrides.servo-constellation/constellation.rs: Edited in the preparation's copied sources after the final patch applied. See engine_override_note.

negative_controls.observed_failure: In both modes, the frames part passes the twelve earlier cases and fails at frame-inactive-parent-failure with 'Unexpected frame failure notices: []'. In multiprocess mode, the processes part passes thirty-two cases and fails at frame-inactive-parent-process-exit with the same error. The documents part passes in every run. All three runs of each mode fail the same way.
negative_controls.interpretation: The inactive parent's frame gets a notice and an error page only because the patch handles a frame whose parent is not the active document. Without it, the closed frame pipeline stays, no notice arrives, and back would restore a parent with a dead frame.

single.scope: Experimental engine scope, host allocation gate, script-thread unwind, final-handle release, explicit engine shutdown, queued execution cancellation, interruption of running JavaScript, content-process exit and forced kill in multiprocess mode, shared-process view revocation and ordinary sibling close, script-thread failure and content-process exit or kill before document construction, crash recovery through reload and history, script-thread failure after response headers and in about:blank, srcdoc, document.write, and document.open() construction, crash recovery of a javascript: URL document to an error page without its result, removal of an inactive javascript: URL history entry during crash recovery, script-thread failure while a cross-site navigation, a cross-site subframe, or a sandboxed srcdoc child parses in its own event loop, content-process exit or kill while a cross-site document, a cross-site subframe, or a sandboxed srcdoc child parses, script-thread failure and content-process exit or kill while a same-site or cross-site child frame's navigation waits for its response headers, containment of a child frame's failure to that frame when the parent's own top-level document runs in another event loop, including a frame's first navigation, a failed frame with a healthy pending navigation, frame history after a contained failure, a failed send to a frame's pipeline, a send that reaches a dead script thread or a killed content process before the panic report or lifeline, several sibling frames that fail together, and a frame inside a failed frame, with one frame failure notice for each surviving view, callback and delegate unwind safety, and constellation loss in a separate engine. Remaining replacement audits remain open.

negative_controls.engine_override_note: The final patch, unchanged on disk. Only the preparation's copied sources/servo-constellation/constellation.rs differs from the final patch result. The runner accepted it because it checks the patch file's hash, not the patched sources.

negative_controls.name: one-entry-per-frame
negative_controls.variation: The final patch, with the check removed that gives each frame at most one entry in contained_failed_frames. A frame whose current pipeline and pending pipeline both fail then gets two entries. Everything else, including the fixture, is final.

engine_overrides.servo-constellation/constellation.rs: Edited in the preparation's copied sources after the final patch applied. See engine_override_note.

negative_controls.observed_failure: In both modes, the frames part passes fourteen cases, including frame-child-navigation-failure, and fails at frame-child-same-site-navigation-failure. The one notice lists the frame twice, once with the current pipeline and once with the pending pipeline. In multiprocess mode, the processes part passes thirty-four cases and fails at frame-child-same-site-navigation-process-exit the same way. The documents part passes in every run. In each mode, all three runs fail the same way. One single-process frames run exited with signal 11 during teardown after printing its error.
negative_controls.interpretation: The same-site case has both pipelines in the failed event loop. Only the patch's one-entry check gives the frame one entry, one notice, and one crash navigation. No earlier case has both pipelines of one frame in the failed event loop, so this control passes them all.

negative_controls.engine_override_note: The final patch, unchanged on disk. Only the preparation's copied sources/servo-constellation/constellation.rs differs from the final patch result. The runner accepted it because it checks the patch file's hash, not the patched sources.

negative_controls.name: traversal-pending-as-history
negative_controls.variation: The final patch, with contained_failed_frames treating a pending pipeline whose change reloads a history entry (replace is a NeedsToReload::Yes) as an inactive history pipeline, not as the frame's failed navigation. Other pending pipelines are unchanged. Everything else, including the fixture, is final.

engine_overrides.servo-constellation/constellation.rs: Edited in the preparation's copied sources after the final patch applied. See engine_override_note.

negative_controls.observed_failure: In both modes, the frames part passes fifteen cases and fails at frame-traversal-failure: the second failure's notice never arrives, and the wait inside the barrier reaches its four-second bound with the first error page still current. In multiprocess mode, the processes part passes thirty-five cases and fails at frame-traversal-process-exit the same way. The documents part passes in every run. In each mode, all three runs fail the same way. One single-process frames run exited with signal 11 during teardown after printing its error.
negative_controls.interpretation: A pending traversal's pipeline fails as the frame's navigation only because the patch treats a pending pipeline of an existing frame as a failed navigation, including one that reloads a history entry. No earlier case has a reloading pending pipeline in a failed event loop, so this control passes every earlier case.

limitations: Multiprocess evidence uses unsandboxed children on macOS arm64 with software rendering.

The inactive parent cases fail the frame's event loop through a popup of the frame's site, because the frame probes read only the active document's frames. The inactive document's own frames are not failed by a frame probe. A frame in a parent that is a future history entry has no fixture.
The notice for a failed frame in an inactive parent is an observed rule that names the active document. The owner has not decided it.

A child frame's navigation of the top-level document, and a child's navigation that its parent started first, have no fixture. A reload of a frame's error page has no fixture, so which load an error page repeats is unchecked for the same-site child navigation.

The pending traversal case needs two failures, because only an entry that must reload can wait for a response. A traversal that waits in the failed event loop together with the frame's current pipeline has no fixture.

In the same-site child navigation case, the notice names either of the frame's two failed pipelines, and the case accepts both. The final runs named the pending pipeline for the unwind and exit and the current pipeline for the kill, and the case marker records the choice. The choice is unspecified, because the constellation's pipelines map is an FxHashMap with unspecified iteration order, and it varied between runs and preparations. The contract does not choose it, and it decides the load data of the frame's error page.

The remaining limitations of the dead event loop checkpoint apply: other send-error callers, a serialization error to a live event loop, a send to a group of frames, and a frame inside a healthy frame have no fixture.
No new Linux, native-input, release-performance, or remote CI evidence is claimed.
